body:
Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368), it works as expected. Code looks good to me.

## Benchmark

<details open>

<summary>PC specifications</summary>

- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
- **RAM:** 64 GB (2×32 GB DDR5-6000 CL30)
- **SSD:** Solidigm P44 Pro 2 TB
- **OS:** Linux (Fedora 42)
</details>

Using a release export template with `production=yes lto=full`.

I can't spot a performance difference in Bunnymark with 500 or 2,000 bunnies, but I can in the dictionary test script (average of 3 runs each):

Type | Before | After
-|-|-
Untyped | 3157 ms | 3189 ms
Typed | 3612 ms | 3533 ms

Typed is definitely slightly faster overall, but it's a toss as to whether untyped is faster or slower than `master`. That said, I still consider this an overall win given we've been increasingly encouraging the use of static typing in GDScript (not just for performance reasons).
